sea_state.notes: Forecast/model (FCT) values from an explicitly selected Open-Meteo model. Model identity, retrieval time and model-run time are recorded so a stale model run can never masquerade as fresh data. Planning context only — not a navigation product and not a go/no-go decision. Hs is significant wave height, NOT the maximum wave height that may be encountered.

tide.note: No approved free/re-distributable automated Channel Islands tide prediction source. Observations are not predictions. Not inferred from global models and NOT derived from sea_level_height_msl (MSL-referenced, limited coastal accuracy, unsuitable for coastal navigation). Official sources must be consulted directly (link-only).

freshness_policy.metadata_policy: model-run provenance from the per-model Open-Meteo metadata document (last_run_initialisation_time) for the SAME pinned model displayed; never derived from retrieval time, forecast validity, cadence, or best_match. Missing metadata => values retained but never fresh (partial).

limitations: Single explicit provider point; no local interpolation by Hermes (brief §7). Provider-side post-processing/interpolation is not disclosed by the API. Model identity is preserved per series — series from different models are never stitched into one homogeneous forecast. Providers are never averaged.
note: Weekend weather + sea-state context for the planner. This snapshot is refreshed ONLY by refresh_conditions.py (updates conditions data, never route geometry). Every value is FCT (forecast/model output) from an explicitly named model, with retrieval + model-run timestamps so freshness is auditable. Tide has no approved source and stays unavailable. Planning context only — not a navigation product and not a go/no-go decision.

spatial_policy.note: Single explicit provider point per dimension; series are reported as returned by the provider for that point.
